DITA KNOWLEDGE (retrieval bundle):
[1] map: <map> is the root element of a DITA map (.ditamap file). It organizes topics into a navigable structure — like a table of contents for your documentation.

What is <map>?
A map does NOT contain content itself. Instead, it references topics via <topicref> and defines their hierarchy, order, and relationships. Maps control navigation (TOC), key definitions, and linking.

Key children:
- <title> — map title
- <topicref> — reference to a topic (the workhorse)
- <topichead> — visible heading without 
---
[2] key-scoping: DITA 1.3 Key Scoping — using the same key name with different values in different parts of a map.

What is Key Scoping?
Key scoping (introduced in DITA 1.3) allows the same key name to resolve to different values depending on where it's used in the map hierarchy. This is done using the @keyscope attribute on <topicref>, <map>, or other map elements.

Why is this useful?
- Reuse the same topic in multiple contexts with different variable values.
- Product-specific content within a shared map stru
---
[3] dita_spec: any specialization of <map> element " or " <topicref> element or any specialization of <topicref> element."
Definitions related to keys
resource
For the purposes of keys and key resolution, one of the following:
• An object addressed by URI
• Metadata specified on a resource, such as a @scope or @format attribute
• Text or metadata located within a <topicmeta> element
key
A name for a resource. See Using keys for addressing (69) for more information.
key definition
A <topicref> element that bind
---
[4] tgroup: <tgroup> is the main structural container inside a CALS <table>. It defines columns, headers, and body rows.

What is <tgroup>?
In the CALS table model (used by DITA's <table> element), <tgroup> wraps the column specifications, optional header, and table body. A <table> can have multiple <tgroup> elements, though one is typical.

Full CALS table structure:
```xml
<table>
  <title>CALS Table Example</title>
  <tgroup cols="3">
    <colspec colname="c1" colwidth="1*"/>
    <colspec colname="c2" co
---

| Feature | choicetable | simpletable | table (CALS) | properties |
|---------|------------|-------------|--------------|------------|
| Purpose | Present choices in a task step | Simple data table | Full-featured table | Property/parameter reference |
| Context | Inside <step> only | Any body content | Any body content | Inside <refbody> only |
| Columns | Always 2 (option + description) | Any nu
---

@rowheader
Indicates whether the entries in the respective column SHOULD be considered row headers. Allowable values are:
firstcol
Indicates that entries in the first column of the table are functionally row headers (analogous to the way that a
<thead> element provides column headers). Applies when @rowheader is used on the <table> element.
headers
Indicates that entries of a column described using the <colspec> element are functionally row headers (for
cases with more than one colu
---

@align
Describes the alignment of text in a table column. Allowable values are:
left
Indicates left alignment of the text.
right
Indicates right alignment of the text.
center
Indicates center alignment of the text.
justify
Justifies the contents to both the left and the right.
char
Use the character specified on the @char attribute for alignment.

---
[8] colspec: <colspec> defines properties for a single column in a CALS <table>. Place one <colspec> per column inside <tgroup>, before <thead> and <tbody>.
